messages:
acme-sre: Hey team, we've been seeing intermittent 503s to our private VPC endpoints since last night's cert renewal. Client error is 'certificate verify failed: unable to get local issuer certificate'. Affects our SDK and curl.

sara: Sorry you're hitting this — can you paste the curl + verbose output and confirm this is only on the VPC/private endpoints (not hosted API)?

acme-sre: Only private. Here's a reduced repro from one of our hosts:
```
$ curl -v https://api.private.acme.internal/health
* Connected to api.private.acme.internal (10.10.5.3) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.2 connection using ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256
* server certificate verification FAILED: unable to get local issuer certificate
* Closing connection 0
```

jamal: Can you run an openssl chain dump for the endpoint? helps confirm the intermediate chain served.

acme-sre: Ran this:
```
$ openssl s_client -connect api.private.acme.internal:443 -showcerts -servername api.private.acme.internal
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=api.private.acme.internal
   i:/CN=AcmeApp-Leaf-CA
 1 s:/CN=AcmeApp-Leaf-CA
   i:/CN=Redwood-Rotator-Intermediate
---
---
No client certificate CA names sent
---
```

acme-sre: The chain stops at our leaf -> leaf CA -> rotator intermediate. Our truststore has the old root CA (AcmeCorp-Root) but the rotator uploaded a cross-signed intermediate yesterday that chains to a different root we don't trust.

sara: Huh. Rotator should have uploaded both the intermediate and the original cross-signing intermediate so both roots work. Jamal, can you check the rotator upload logs?

rotator-bot: Upload job 2026-03-16T03:01:12Z started for tenant acme-corp
rotator-bot: Fetched renewed cert from ACME provider (status: VALID)
rotator-bot: Assembled bundle with 2 certs, uploaded to s3://rotator-bundles/acme/2026-03-16
rotator-bot: POST /internal/ca-bundles returned 200 OK
rotator-bot: NOTE: intermediate file size 0 bytes for acme-cross-signed.pem (skipping)

jamal: That "0 bytes" stands out. Looks like the bundling step skipped the cross-signed intermediate due to an empty temp file. Could be intermittent S3 read glitch or ACME provider returned unexpected multipart.

mike: Also check networking — our rotator fetches OCSP/AIA during assembly. If the customer egress allowlist blocks acme-challenge or the CA AIA fetch, the rotator may leave a partial chain. Any firewall logs?

acme-sre: We did recently tighten outbound firewall rules for VPC workers — could be blocking rotator egress to acme-issuer.example.com. I can open a ticket to temporarily allow it.

jamal: In the short term we can replace the bundle with a repaired one (include both intermediates). Steps:
1) acme-sre to confirm PEMs for leaf + both intermediates and upload to us via secure upload
2) we validate chain with `openssl verify -CAfile <root>.pem bundle.pem`
3) update the private endpoint with the full bundle and trigger envoy reload.

sara: For longer term, we'll add a rotator validation check: after bundling, run `openssl verify` against both known roots and fail the job if the chain is incomplete. Also add a retry on empty intermediate downloads.

acme-sre: Uploading the intermediates now to the support upload link. Also we'll open a firewall change to allow the rotator outbound to acme-issuer.example.com:443 and ocsp endpoints.

mike: After you upload, I'll validate and push a hotfix to the endpoint. Expect a brief reload — I'll schedule during your low-traffic window. :thumbsup:

acme-sre: Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround. One question: could client SDKs keep failing after we push the full chain because of cached old trust anchors? Some clients do pin the old root cert in their local JVM keystore.

jamal: Good call. If clients are pinning a single root, they'll need to trust the new chain or we must ensure the bundle chains to the old root as well. The repaired bundle will include the original root path (cross-signed intermediate) so pinned clients should continue to work.

sara: Follow-ups: jamal to add rotator validation + retry, mike to coordinate reload with acme-sre, acme-sre to update firewall and confirm upload. I'll create a short postmortem note after resolution.

acme-sre: Uploaded bundle and confirmed the firewall rule change (egress to acme-issuer allowed). Will stand by.

jamal: I pulled the upload, ran verification: `openssl verify -CAfile /tmp/AcmeCorp-Roots.pem /tmp/repaired-bundle.pem` -> OK chaining to both roots. Deploying now and triggering envoy reload.

mike: Reload done. Can you retry the curl?

acme-sre: Curl now returns 200 and SDK traffic looks healthy. No more verification errors. Thanks all. :tada:

sara: Closing as resolved. We'll track rotator validation in the next sprint.
